info.bio:
Richard Meyers (Lexington, Kentucky, Estados Unidos, 2 de octubre de 1949), mejor conocido como Richard Hell, es un cantante, compositor, bajista y escritor reconocido mundialmente por haber sido el líder de la influyente banda de la primera ola del punk The Voidoids y el bajista del grupo proto-punk Television.

Hell suele ser considerado como el primer músico en utilizar la imagen punk del cabello en punta, la ropa destrozada y los alfileres de gancho para sostenerla.

scenes.name: Punk neoyorquino del CBGB
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Ramones, Television, Patti Smith, Blondie, The Heartbreakers: una escena que, como advirtió James Wolcott en 1975 («Un impulso conservador en el nuevo underground del rock»), se presentaba como el retorno de algo perdido. Los Ramones agotan su idea en dos discos, los Heartbreakers son Dr. Feelgood con heroína y hasta Television bebe del acid rock de la costa oeste. La revista Punk de Legs McNeil proclama «¡Muerte a esa mierda disco!» y rechaza al hipster como «negro blanco».

scenes.name: New wave neoyorquina
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: 1976 es un año bisagra: los sellos independientes revitalizan la industria y nuevos géneros la escena, una revolución comparable a la de 1966. Los jóvenes de los setenta, sin sueños tras la derrota de la contracultura, canalizan su aburrimiento en un sonido crudo emparentado con el garage. Nueva York es la capital: el CBGB's y el Max's Kansas City. Patti Smith, Richard Hell (el profeta: «Blank Generation» y la ética punk), Television (Marquee Moon, que define la estética de la new wave), Tom Verlaine, y los Ramones, que tocan rock'n'roll inepto a velocidad supersónica e inventan el género más importante del último cuarto de siglo.

podcast.title: Connection to Sex Pistols' Origins
podcast.body: Inspired by Richard Hell's fashion, Malcolm McLaren used the safety pin aesthetic at his London store, Sex, and eventually conceived the idea of forming a band, the Sex Pistols, to act as a living advertisement for the shop. "McLaren then imported Richard's safety pin look back to Britain and opened a clothing shop that sold these kinds of clothes. The store became a magnet for young, disaffected kids. And to promote his store, Malcolm came up with the idea of forming a band that would be a living, breathing advertisement for the place. This store was called Sex. And the name of this band would be the Sex Pistols."

podcast.title: Early Life and Artistic Path
podcast.body: Richard Hell, born Richard Myers in Kentucky, initially moved to New York with the ambition of becoming a poet before becoming captivated by the burgeoning punk scene at CBGB. "Richard, his real name was Richard Myers, was a member of several New York punk bands who hung out at CBGB, the brilliant television and the heartbreakers featuring the doomed Johnny Thunders, ex of the New York dolls. Richard was born in Kentucky but moved to New York with plans of being a poet."

podcast.title: Formation of The Voidoids
podcast.body: Richard Hell grew dissatisfied with The Heartbreakers and decided to form his own band, The Voidoids, a nihilistic punk group. The band's name was taken from a novel Richard was writing at the time. "But back to Richard. He grew tired of the heartbreakers very quickly and decided he needed to front his own band. They became known as the Voidoy's, a nihilistic punk group. The name came from the title of a novel Richard was working on at the time."

podcast.title: Influence on Punk Fashion
podcast.body: Richard Hell's distinctive safety-pin-adorned clothing caught the attention of UK band manager Malcolm McLaren in New York. McLaren subsequently brought this "safety pin look" to Britain, incorporating it into his clothing shop "Sex," which became a popular spot for disaffected youth. "So Richard wore his clothes until they fell apart. In fact, he wore them even after they fell apart, holding things together with safety pins. This went a wannabe band manager from the UK named Malcolm McLaren, saw Richard in New York and thought he had brilliant fashion sense."

podcast.title: New York Punk Scene Fixture
podcast.body: The Voidoids were a significant band on the New York punk scene in the middle 1970s. They embodied the experimental, often non-commercial, and anti-materialistic art statement that defined early North American punk. "Richard Hell and The Voidoids, a fixture on the New York punk scene in the middle 1970s."
